IS t 5943 -1970 



Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 
COMPOUND ANGLE SINE TABLES 



( Reaffirmed 2006 ) 



1. Scope — This standard covers the requirements of a sine table inclinable to 60° about two axes with 
centre distances of rollers 100 mm at top and 200 mm at bottom. 

2. Essential Features — These are a base provided with a slip gauge platform and an Intermediate table 
with a setting roller at one end and a hinge roller at the other end. Alternately, both rollers of the 
Intermediate table could be such that any one of the rollers could be used for setting, thereby enabling 
the intermediate table to tilt in both ways. This table has slip gauge platform prependicular to that 
on base. A work table with a setting roller at one end and hinge roller at other end is positioned per- 
pendicular to the intermediate table. At least one end and one side stop shall be provided on the work 
table. The height of the slip gauge platforms shall be such as to require the insertion of setting slip 
gauges in order to bring the upper surface of the work table parallel with the base. T-slots or a magnetic 
face for clamping of workpieces shall be provided on the work table. Compound angle sine tables are 
used as a clamping fixture for precise machining operations, such as for grinding (see Fig. I and 2).

IS: 5943- 1970 

4.1 The setting of the compound angle sine table sfc&H not differ from the nominal by more than 0*2 
minutes of arc over the entire range of setting. 

5. Types — The following types are covered: 

Type A — Work table of magnetic face. 
Type B— Work table with T-slots. 

6. Designation — The compound angie sine tables shaii be designated by type, size and the number of 
this standard* 

Example : 

Compound Angle Sine Table A 320 x 160 IS : S943 

7. General Requirements 

7.1 Material— Base, tables, stops, rollers are made of high quality case-carburising steel or close- 
grained cast iron suitably heat-treated. 

7.2 Hardness — The working surfaces, rollers, slip gauge platfqrqrt, and end and side stops shall have a 
hardness of not less than 700 HV [see IS : ISO 1-1968 Tlethod for Vickers hardness test for steel (first 
revision) 9 ] while the base shall have a hardness of not less^han 650 HV (see IS : 1501-1968). 

7.3 Surface Roughness — This shall be as specified in Table 3, 



TABLE 3 SURFACE ROUGHNESS 

Surfaces Surface Roughness 

Ra in pm 

Cylindrical surfaces of rollers 0*2 

Top surface of work table 0'2 

Slip gauge platform 005 

End-and-side stops ( surface towards 0*2 

work table) 



7.4 Rigidity— The sine table shall be sufficiently rigid so that the maximum deflection of work table under 
a vertical central load of 10 kg shall not exceed 3/xm. 

7.5 The T-slots or tapped holes, if provided, shall be placed symmetrically with respect to the axes of 
the work table and no T-slot or tapped hole shall be provided within 30 mm from the edge of the table. 
The T-stots shall conform to*IS:20l 3-1 962' Dimensions for T-slots' and the threading of the tapped holes 
shad conform to iS: 4218-1967 • iSO metric screw threads'. The number and the exact positioning of 
the T-slots or tapped holes is left to the option of the designer. 

8. Packing and Storage — All surfaces of sine table shall be protected against climatic conditions by 
giving a suitable anticorrosion treatment. 

9. Marking— Each compound angie sine table shall be marked with the following information: 

a) Work table size and centre distances of tof. and bottom rollers, 

b) Setting slip gauge dimensions, and 

c) Manufacturer's trade name or mark. 

9A Certification Marking — Details available with the Bureau of Indian Standards.
